analysis.subject: computing
analysis.pageCoverage: The page defines binary search on a sorted array by halving the interval, states the middle calculation and an overflow-safe alternative, notes logarithmic time with linear traversals versus logarithmic comparisons on a linked list, and lists related search methods.

overview.headline: Binary search by halving a sorted interval

keyPoints.point: Students learn that binary search operates on a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the interval in half.
keyPoints.quote: Search a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that if the search key is less than the middle item the interval narrows to the lower half and otherwise to the upper half.
keyPoints.quote: If the value of the search key is less than the item in the middle of the interval, narrow the interval to the lower half.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that binary search on an ordered linked list still needs linear traversals but performs only logarithmic comparisons.
keyPoints.quote: It makes O(n) traversals, as does linear search, but it only performs O(log n) comparisons.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the midpoint calculation can overflow when high and low are near the largest expressible integer and a safe alternative exists.
keyPoints.quote: This overflows if high and low are close to the largest expressible integer.

keyTerms.gloss: Ordered array where binary search repeatedly divides the search interval
keyTerms.quote: Search a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.

keyTerms.gloss: Current search interval that begins covering the whole array and then narrows
keyTerms.quote: Begin with an interval covering the whole array.

keyTerms.gloss: General strategy that uses divide to break a problem into smaller parts
Failure when calculation exceeds the largest expressible integer for high and low
keyTerms.quote: This overflows if high and low are close to the largest expressible integer.

keyTerms.gloss: Checks of the search key against middle items that the search performs
keyTerms.quote: It makes O(n) traversals, as does linear search, but it only performs O(log n) comparisons.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Tracing the halving steps shows how the interval narrows to find a target in sorted data.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Search a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Cards reinforce runtime, overflow avoidance and the difference between traversals and comparisons.
componentPlan.focusQuote: This overflows if high and low are close to the largest expressible integer.
